extractor.note: Partial pass over the Introduction and Chapter I, where the three components of the phenomenological method — reduction, construction, destruction — are set out.

coverage_note: Covers the Introduction and Chapter I, 'The Question of Being'. The later chapters on space are not covered.

units.claim: The incompletion of Sein und Zeit is not explained by obstacles in the phenomenological destruction of the tradition, much of which Heidegger had already accomplished.
units.quote: Does the incompletion mean that the *phenomenological destruction of the tradition* presented insurmountable obstacles that forbade its execution?

units.claim: The relation of being to the essence of the human being is inaccessible without a displacement and reduction of consciousness, since from consciousness things cannot be reached in their worldliness.
units.quote: inaccessible without the *displacement and reduction of consciousness* (because from consciousness it is impossible to reach things in their very being, i.e. in their *worldliness*)

units.claim: As transcendental subjectivity covered over by the psyche surges forth in its own being thanks to the reduction, so Dasein initially understands itself from out of the world of things.
units.quote: Just as, according to Husserl, *transcendental subjectivity* — covered over by the *psyche* (ψυχή) — surges forth in its own being *thanks to the reduction* (the psyche being only its *mundanization*)

units.claim: The phenomenological reduction is defined as the leading-back of the inquiring gaze from naively grasped beings toward being.
units.quote: the fundamental component of the phenomenological method, in the sense of the *leading-back of the inquiring gaze from naively grasped beings toward being*, is what is designated *phenomenological reduction*

units.claim: This reduction shares with Husserl's transcendental reduction only the purely formal trait of a conversion of the gaze, and nothing of its content.
units.quote: this reduction shares with Husserl's *transcendental* reduction *only the purely formal trait* of a *conversion of the gaze* — and nothing of its content

units.claim: The second component is phenomenological construction, the projection of the pre-given being with regard to its being and ontological structures.
units.quote: The *projection of the pre-given being*, with regard to its being and its ontological structures, is what is called *phenomenological construction*.

units.claim: The third component is destruction, required because the history of ontology covers over the possibility of fundamental-ontological construction as a forgetting of the first experiences of being.
units.quote: The history of ontology *covers over* the possibility of fundamental-ontological construction; it constitutes a *forgetting of the first experiences of being* that lie at the origin of metaphysics.
